newsitem.title: UK: Major agrees to TV debate with Blair-party.
newsitem.headline: Major agrees to TV debate with Blair-party.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major has agreed to go ahead with television debates with opposition leader Tony Blair in the run-up to a May 1 general election, his Conservative Party said on Wednesday.
Blair's Labour Party has been pressing for the debates, along the lines of those held in the U.S. presidential election, and Major recently indicated he favoured the idea.
A Conservative spokeswoman said Major had instructed a senior party official to begin negotiations over the debates with both the British Broadcasting Corporation and Independent Television.
Both companies have put forward proposals for two 90-minute debates between the two leaders during the election campaign.
But the minority Liberal Democrats have objected, saying their leader, Paddy Ashdown, must be allowed to take part under rules giving the major parties equal airtime during the election campaign.

The Conservative official would try to agree with the television companies a formula that would be in keeping with the election guidelines, while allowing a head-to-head debate between Major and Blair, the spokeswoman said.
With few major policy differences between the two main parties, the debates will highlight the great gulf in style between the two leaders.
Major's lack of charisma has earned him the title "the grey man of politics", but the Conservatives see his very "ordinariness" as their greatest asset.
His personal opinion poll ratings have persistently exceeded those of his own party, while many voters are suspicious of Blair's slick presentation.

Labour is currently around 25 points ahead of the Conservatives in opinion polls, but Major says he is confident he can win the election with his personal style of campaigning from a battered soapbox.
